rule: GOAL: Match the top color sequence by filling the middle slots in order. CONTROLS: Click a bottom color to select it, then click a middle slot to place it. RULE: Slots must match the left-to-right order of the colored frames above. TRAP: Thinking any arrangement works; only the exact top order clears the level.

GOAL: Slide the charcoal plug rightward to align it with the target gap. CONTROLS: The top blue button moves the plug right; the bottom blue button moves it left. RULE: Each click shifts the plug four columns at a time, requiring precise alignment. TRAP: Believing the buttons adjust the background or wall position instead of moving the plug itself.

GOAL: Move the purple orb along the trail to reach the core. CONTROLS: Click any dot within three steps to swap the orb there. RULE: Dots remain on all trail positions except the orb’s current spot. TRAP: Assuming the core is a standard dot; it may not be clickable until adjacent.

GOAL: Align the plug's green section vertically with the gap in the bar. CONTROLS: Click below-top to raise the middle edge and lower the top edge; click below-bottom to raise the bottom edge and lower the middle edge. RULE: The bottom edge cannot exceed the middle edge by more than twenty units, and no edge can drop below zero. TRAP: Believing you could shift the bottom edge indefinitely without first raising the middle edge to maintain the required balance.

GOAL: Fill the castle notch with liquid while shielding the ground from any spillage. CONTROLS: Arrows move the blocking bar; space releases the liquid flow. RULE: The level clears only if the liquid fills the target without touching the ground surface. TRAP: Believing you must block every gap; you only need to shield the specific landing zones.

GOAL: Guide the split block through the stepped shaft to the handle. CONTROLS: Arrow keys slide the block; it moves until hitting a wall or step. RULE: The tall section only fits the wide corridor; you must climb to the thin upper path to reach the start. TRAP: Thinking the block slides freely everywhere; it gets stuck trying to move left in the lower rows without going up first.

GOAL: Clear the level by moving the piece 28 times. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the piece one step in the chosen direction. RULE: You must count every single keypress to track your progress toward the goal. TRAP: Do not assume the puzzle geometry changes; the top section remains static, so focus only on movement count.

GOAL: Arrange colored blocks into a specific sequence to unlock the exit. CONTROLS: Click a filled slot to pick up its block, then click another slot to swap their contents. Press space to validate the arrangement. RULE: Blocks must follow a strict order, with red pieces framing the green sequence. TRAP: Clicking an empty slot wastes moves; you must select a filled slot first to initiate a swap.

GOAL: Shrink the block and navigate it upward through a narrow gate to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; clicks select matching keypad cells to trigger the shrink. RULE: The block must match the reference pattern’s color and position to shrink before passing through the two-cell-wide gate. TRAP: Trying to push the full-sized block through the gate wastes time; it physically cannot fit until the keypad match shrinks it.

GOAL: Raise plugs to specific heights to connect sockets, leaving empty spaces between bars and platforms. CONTROLS: Side buttons transfer height between adjacent columns, moving fluid from one platform to the next. RULE: Total height is conserved; only relative differences matter, so focus on final target levels rather than absolute positions. TRAP: Assuming buttons add height independently; they actually subtract from neighbors, requiring careful order to avoid negative values.

GOAL: Fill seven slots to spell the target word using the correct colors. CONTROLS: Click palette colors to assign them to specific empty slots. RULE: Insert colors into slots in left-to-right order, skipping blocked positions. TRAP: Assuming all slots are accessible; some are blocked by rings and must be skipped.

GOAL: Align the plug with the socket by setting all buttons to the Blue state. CONTROLS: Click button caps and stems to toggle their color between White and Blue. RULE: Blue-Blue button combinations consistently move the plug downward toward the target. TRAP: Assuming White buttons contribute to the solution wastes time; only Blue states drive progress.

GOAL: Place three cargo boxes onto the designated bar to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player; SPACE picks up or drops the cargo. RULE: While carrying, the cargo stays locked to your left side, so you must approach targets from the right. TRAP: Assuming rotation happens while moving. Turning only occurs when stationary; moving while carrying keeps the stripe fixed left.

GOAL: Fill red and green boxes to match the top frame's sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, click slots to place, space to confirm. RULE: The ring acts as a bridge, letting green slots fit between red ones to complete the pattern. TRAP: Assuming the ring fits anywhere; it only works at specific junctions to align both colors.

GOAL: Map four pink slots to seven yellow slots by matching glyph sequences. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; UP cycles carousel patterns to align glyphs. RULE: Pink slot lengths must sum exactly to the total yellow slot count. TRAP: Assuming all yellow slots are valid targets wastes time on distractor pairs.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to reach the green target tile. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player two spaces per press. RULE: A move succeeds only if both the intermediate and final tiles are open floor. TRAP: Assuming inputs register instantly causes failures; wait for animations to finish before sending the next command.

GOAL: Fit colored blocks and rings into matching slots to complete the pattern. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select, click slots to place, press space to confirm. RULE: Ring colors must match slot borders, while solid blocks match slot interiors. TRAP: Assuming duplicate identical blocks are interchangeable without checking specific slot constraints.

GOAL: Align sliding color tiles to match fixed reference patterns and open the door. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor and adjust slot values; action confirms each alignment. RULE: The left tile color marks the fixed row; the right tile color marks the adjustable row. TRAP: Assuming the cursor moves linearly rather than wrapping cyclically wastes actions on long adjustments.

GOAL: Place three rings and six solids into red and colored boxes to match the top sequence. CONTROLS: Click palette items, then click slots. Press Space to check. RULE: Each box’s first item must be its own color; the top sequence splits into triples where the first element identifies the box color. TRAP: Assuming any ring order works. The rings must match the first element of each triple to correctly assign the remaining solids.

GOAL: Map the source symbols to the final output symbols using the intermediate rules. CONTROLS: Use the arrow keys to select the target slots and confirm the correct mapping for each position. RULE: Follow the chain from source to intermediate, then intermediate to final, ensuring every link matches exactly. TRAP: Assuming all symbols map directly without checking if the intermediate symbol actually exists as a rule input.

GOAL: Place rings to expand colored boxes, forming a target sequence by inserting one box into another. CONTROLS: Click palette items to select; click board slots to place rings or solids; press space to submit the solution. RULE: A ring’s color dictates which box it inserts into the current slot, expanding the sequence at that position. TRAP: Believing rings can be placed anywhere; they must go into empty slots of the correct box to trigger the specific expansion needed.

ESTABLISHED: R, b, and N exist at specific coordinates. The rope attaches blocks when aligned correctly. FAILED: Moving the N to column 24 while attached failed to secure the final position without interference. GOAL IS NOT: Simply dragging blocks left in any order; sequence determines stacking success. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the handle; the rope drags attached blocks. Release requires retracting the rope fully.

GOAL: Reach the exit by passing the red enemy without colliding with its charge. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player one step in that direction. RULE: The red enemy only charges horizontally within two cells on its row; vertical approaches are safe. TRAP: Assuming the red tile is a solid wall; landing on it is actually safe and collects the item.

GOAL: Position each cross center where its row and column arms align with matching dots. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active cross three spaces per press; space switched between crosses. RULE: Centers had to sit at the intersection of shared rows and columns for all four dots. TRAP: Assuming you needed to cover every dot individually rather than aligning axes simultaneously.

GOAL: Reach the exit by collecting the red tile. CONTROLS: Arrows move one step. RULE: The red tile only charges along its row; approach from below to collect it safely. TRAP: Believing the red tile is an immovable wall or instant death on contact; landing on it removes it.

GOAL: Rotate the ring to align the yellow block with the bracketed slot. CONTROLS: Click the red arrow to rotate the ring counter-clockwise. RULE: Each click shifts the ring one position; yellow must reach the fixed target. TRAP: Assuming complex color matching or pathfinding; the goal was simply positional alignment.

GOAL: Extend bars to touch plus signs. CONTROLS: Click frames to grow bars. RULE: Each click extends the bar by three units. TRAP: Assuming clicks only move the tail; the whole bar grows, so count total length, not just the tip.

GOAL: Place the purple blob onto the purple ring target. CONTROLS: Click to move the head; click the anchor to swap head and anchor positions. RULE: The blob always sits exactly at the midpoint between the head and the anchor. TRAP: Thinking you can drag the blob directly; you must position both endpoints to force the center onto the ring.

GOAL: Transport the diamond to its target slot before the energy bar empties. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active object; Space toggles between the player and the diamond. RULE: The energy bar drains over real time, not just per action, so speed matters more than step count. TRAP: Believing the bar only drops when you press a key, causing you to hesitate and waste precious seconds.

GOAL: Cover all seven dots using three distinct shapes: an X, a horizontal line, and a diamond. CONTROLS: Arrows move the active shape; Space switches to the next shape in the cycle. RULE: Each shape covers specific dots only when positioned at precise coordinates where its geometry aligns with the targets. TRAP: Assuming the line has a vertical arm; it is horizontal-only, so vertical positioning matters less than horizontal alignment.

GOAL: Clear the board by jumping pegs over neighbors to capture them. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it and reveal valid jump destinations, then click a destination to execute the move. RULE: A jump requires an adjacent peg and an empty space immediately beyond it in a straight line. TRAP: Capturing the wrong piece early can isolate remaining pegs, making them impossible to capture or move.

GOAL: Align both yellow blocks to the target column on the right side. CONTROLS: Red A rotates the outer loop; Red B shifts the middle row; Red C shifts the bottom row. RULE: Blocks at shared intersections move with either the loop or the row, depending on the last action. TRAP: Assuming the yellow blocks move independently of the conveyor belts when they sit on shared cells.

GOAL: Move the green bar into the yellow frame to trigger completion. CONTROLS: Click sky to raise green, yellow to shift it right, green to shrink its tail. RULE: Bars move as rigid blocks; the dot must align with the target center. TRAP: Thinking the green tail could pass through the yellow frame to shorten the path.

GOAL: Guide the black block into the left ring socket. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the active block; clicking swaps which block is active. RULE: Blocks stop immediately upon the first overlap of their bounding boxes. TRAP: Thinking blocks pass through rings freely; they stop at the ring's outer edge, not its center.

GOAL: Move the yellow token to the yellow bracket and the orange token to the orange bracket. CONTROLS: Click red buttons to shift tokens forward along the loops; click green buttons to shift them backward. RULE: Red and green actions are perfect inverses, allowing you to undo any move instantly. TRAP: Do not assume loops are independent; they share cells, so moving one token affects the other’s path.

GOAL: Align the dial to match the marker, then enter the box. CONTROLS: Arrows move the block; toggling changes the dial state. RULE: The marker becomes passable only when the dial perfectly matches its orientation. TRAP: Believing you can enter the box while the dial is misaligned wastes turns.

GOAL: Flip the large grid cells so their colors match the exact negative of the static mini-grid pattern, turning specific cells red or blue to align with the target mask. CONTROLS: Clicking a large cell toggles its color between red and blue, directly changing the panel's state to meet the completion condition. RULE: The puzzle is solved only when every large cell's color is the opposite of the corresponding mini-grid indicator, requiring precise matching. TRAP: Assuming a cell was already correct without verifying the full pattern caused wasted clicks, as one required red cell was overlooked

GOAL: Paint specific grid cells red to match the pattern hidden by the key. CONTROLS: Click empty cells to toggle their color between blue and red. RULE: Where the key shows gray, paint blue; where it shows white, paint red. TRAP: Ignoring the key’s color mapping and guessing cell states randomly wastes clicks.

ESTABLISHED: The maze layout is dynamic; cell (1,9) shifted from open to wall without direct block interaction, contradicting static assumptions. FAILED: Repeatedly moving blocks to top positions and attempting to map static coordinates, assuming walls remain fixed regardless of block placement. GOAL IS NOT: A fixed geometric path or a static map where walls only exist as initial obstacles independent of block movement. CONTROLS: Moving blocks alters the maze structure itself, changing which cells are passable or blocked, not just occupying space.

GOAL: Cover the target area with a plus-shaped pattern to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the cursor; SPACE activates the current tool. RULE: The tool only works when its center aligns with a valid fill cell. TRAP: Assuming any nearby position covers enough cells wastes time; precise centering is required.

GOAL: Align both blocks at the top center of the arch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved both blocks simultaneously in opposite directions. RULE: Blocks merge into a single unit when they become adjacent. TRAP: Believing the top row was the finish line, ignoring the need to merge first.

GOAL: Guide the yellow block to the center and the orange block to the exit corner. CONTROLS: Left and Right shift the top row; Down and Up shift the side column. RULE: The blocks move along a fixed circular track shared by the row and column. TRAP: Assuming rows and columns move independently wastes time; they are linked at the corners.

ESTABLISHED: Blue player starts top-left; goal is bottom-right alcove. Red snake is a static wall. White cells are walls; black cells are paths. FAILED: Pressing SPACE toggles the HUD icons but does not move the second entity or solve the puzzle. GOAL IS NOT: Activating the ghost entity or interacting with the second HUD icon. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the blue player one cell per press. SPACE toggles the active HUD indicator only.

GOAL: Align the plug's red tips with the socket terminals to complete the circuit. CONTROLS: Arrow keys shift the plug grid to position it within the socket. RULE: The action bar decreases with every move, demanding precise, efficient positioning. TRAP: Assuming large steps is risky; verify the exact pixel movement per press to avoid wasting the limited action budget.

GOAL: Place four blocks into matching rings. CONTROLS: Arrows move selected block; click selects it. RULE: Match block size to ring interior. TRAP: Clicking any block moves it; ensure correct selection before moving.

GOAL: Move two yellow blocks onto the two top-row bracket cells. CONTROLS: Top arrows shift only the top row; side arrows rotate the entire large loop. RULE: The top row is part of the big loop, so side moves also shift top blocks. TRAP: Assuming top and side controls are independent wastes turns; they share cells, so order matters.

GOAL: Recolor two shapes by dragging swatches over them. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Space toggles between shapes. RULE: Shapes change color only when fully covered by a matching swatch. TRAP: Assuming crossing shapes recolor each other; they do not, so ignore overlaps and focus solely on swatch placement.

GOAL: Flip every cell to match the hidden target pattern. CONTROLS: Click cells to toggle their color. RULE: Match the dot's color on white keys, and the opposite on gray keys. TRAP: Hesitating to verify the target first, wasting time on long deliberations that drain the timer bar.

GOAL: Guide the snake to the exit while navigating obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrows move the snake; Space resets position and toggles a replaying ghost. RULE: The ghost replays your path, advancing one step for every move you make. TRAP: Assuming the ghost is static; it moves in sync with you, potentially blocking your path or triggering switches unexpectedly.

GOAL: Slide the two blocks together so they merge into a single shape across the divider. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved both blocks simultaneously in the same direction. RULE: Blocks stop moving when they touch the divider wall or each other. TRAP: Believing you could push blocks through the divider or separate them once joined.

GOAL: Recolor all target cells to match the level's specific color pattern. CONTROLS: Clicking a cell cycles its color; some colors require multiple clicks to reach the target hue. RULE: Each cell must land exactly on the designated color, with orange targets needing two clicks from the start. TRAP: Assuming one click suffices for all colors; failing to double-click orange cells leaves them incomplete.

ESTABLISHED: Green rides the red piece's rotation about the darkred corner, moving from the red's left end to its top. The blue swap triggers a refusal wave and resets the board. FAILED: Clicking the blue piece causes a diagonal wave animation followed by a complete revert, wasting bar. GOAL IS NOT: The blue piece is not the vehicle for transport; it acts as a static blocker or trap. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the green piece. Clicking the red piece rotates it counter-clockwise. Clicking blue attempts an illegal swap.

GOAL: Reach the yellow dot to free it. CONTROLS: Arrows move; clicks toggle colored bars between horizontal and vertical. RULE: You can only stand on a color when that bar is flat under you. TRAP: Thinking you could cross a vertical bar; you must toggle it flat first.

GOAL: Reach the exit without colliding with the patrolling orange. CONTROLS: Arrows move you one step; the orange moves two steps in its facing direction. RULE: The orange bounces off walls, reversing its facing direction upon hitting a boundary. TRAP: Assuming the orange chases you; it ignores your position, moving purely by inertia and wall bounces.

ESTABLISHED: The white region forms a tapered lens shape in the lower-left, bounded by diagonal edges. FAILED: Attempting to fill the target directly with the upper-left stamp colors unwanted upper rows. GOAL IS NOT: A simple half-split of the canvas; the boundary is strictly diagonal, not horizontal. CONTROLS: Arrow keys rotate the stamp footprint around the center. Space applies the selected color to the current footprint area.

GOAL: Paint the top half white and the bottom half purple. CONTROLS: Arrows move the stamp to specific angles, clicks choose ink colors, and Space paints the visible region. RULE: The stamp only paints the shape currently facing the camera, so you must rotate to the correct angle before pressing Space. TRAP: Believing you can paint the whole canvas at once wastes turns; you must split the work between the upright and tilted positions.

GOAL: Fill the canvas with purple above and orange below the diagonal line. CONTROLS: SPACE stamps the current color; RIGHT and DOWN rotate the stamp; clicking icons selects colors. RULE: The stamp rotates in 45-degree increments, changing which side of the diagonal it covers. TRAP: Pressing DOWN from the home position does nothing; you must rotate RIGHT first to reach the needed angle.

ESTABLISHED: The bubble is five columns wide, while the sprite is three. Vertical shafts require exact alignment for the bubble to pass. Horizontal blocks carve five columns, but land blocks carve six. FAILED: Assuming the sprite alone determines collision. Assuming the bubble can pass through misaligned shafts. GOAL IS NOT: A simple alignment puzzle where the sprite position dictates the bubble position. CONTROLS: Clicking blocks carves water. Left and right move the sprite. The bubble follows the sprite's center.

GOAL: Navigate to the exit while managing two snakes and their ghost records. CONTROLS: Arrows move the player; Space records a path, clears ghosts, and resets the active snake slot. RULE: Pressing Space creates a ghost that replays your recent moves, holding buttons down to keep gates open for your next run. TRAP: Do not assume ghosts vanish automatically; they persist until Space is pressed again to clear them and reset the recording cycle.

GOAL: Navigate the grid from start to finish in minimal steps. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move your character one cell at a time. RULE: Only land on valid cells; obstacles block your path entirely. TRAP: Assuming the previous cell alone identifies your state ignores time or direction, causing loops or errors.

GOAL: Float the bubble to the top pool by clearing the path. CONTROLS: Arrows slide the bubble horizontally; clicking blocks removes them. RULE: The bubble always rises to the highest water level in its current column. TRAP: Thinking you must press a direction to rise after clearing the block; the bubble floats up automatically once the path opens.

GOAL: Place three yellow blocks into their matching bracket slots simultaneously. CONTROLS: Click arrows to rotate spokes or rings; click center to swap all three blocks at once. RULE: The center swap only works when all three blocks are already at the swap points. TRAP: Filling one bracket early prevents others; you must position all blocks before triggering the final swap.

GOAL: Align the plug's yellow tip with the gate bottom and match adjacent platform heights to unlock the path. CONTROLS: Click left or right bar edges to raise one platform while lowering its paired partner. RULE: Gates only open when the plug aligns vertically and neighboring platforms sit at equal levels. TRAP: Pressing the wrong side of a bar lowers the target platform instead of raising it, forcing wasted reset clicks.

GOAL: Align the key's halves to match the door's pattern, then slide the tip into the head's core. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the key one step; clicking a column rotated or shifted specific sections. RULE: The key only fits when its colored segments perfectly mirror the door's locked state. TRAP: Assuming the head's interior was always walkable; it was blocked by matching colors until the door opened.

GOAL: Move the yellow block from the left bracket to the right bracket while keeping the other yellow block in place. CONTROLS: Green arrows shift blocks right or up; red arrows shift blocks left or down. RULE: Horizontal blocks cycle through the main row, while vertical blocks rotate through the side column, allowing you to swap positions. TRAP: Thinking the side column was irrelevant caused wasted moves; it is essential for swapping blocks in the main row.

GOAL: Move the block to cover the plus button and collect rings to refill your action bar. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block; stepping on the plus rotates the dial; stepping on rings refills actions. RULE: The dial cycles through shapes; you must land on the plus until the dial shows the target shape to clear. TRAP: The plus button reappears after you leave, allowing repeated presses, but the action bar drains fast if you miss ring pickups.

GOAL: Guide the green block to the yellow target using exactly eleven moves. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block two spaces per press. RULE: The block only stops on open, flat ground. TRAP: Assuming the red barrier stays open permanently wastes time; it may reset if you leave the trigger plate.

ESTABLISHED: The wall rises with the orange when the green bar grows. The sky bar stops at column 44 due to the block. FAILED: Growing the green bar without clearing the wall blocks the sky bar. The sky bar cannot reach the target if the wall remains low. GOAL IS NOT: Simply extending the sky bar. The wall must move up first to clear the path for the sky bar's tail. CONTROLS: Green grows to lift the orange and wall. Red shrinks to lower the wall. Sky and pink bars extend to reach targets.

GOAL: Guide the yellow square to the target zone without overlapping obstacles. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the square one grid step per press. RULE: The square cannot pass through charcoal boxes; only open space is traversable. TRAP: Assuming you can reverse mid-path; backtracking wastes moves, so commit to one direction per segment.

GOAL: Capture all red targets by moving perpendicular to their facing direction. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move one step; entering a square from the side captures the target. RULE: You can only capture a target if you enter its square from the left or right, never from above or below. TRAP: Moving straight into a target fails; you must approach from the side, requiring careful routing to avoid being blocked.

GOAL: Move the head to collect nodes and align them with target rings using only six actions. CONTROLS: Click empty spaces to move the head; click nodes to swap positions and colors. RULE: Nodes of the same color merge into a single group at their shared center. TRAP: Moving the head without swapping first separates groups, making alignment impossible within the move limit.

GOAL: Reach the exit at the bottom right while avoiding lethal red guards. CONTROLS: Arrows move one step; side-entry captures guards. RULE: Guards kill only in their facing direction, not from the side. TRAP: Entering a guard's front row kills you; capture from below first.

GOAL: Reach the exit box by managing a depleting action bar through refills. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the character; interacting with rings replenishes the bar. RULE: Collecting rings instantly restores actions, allowing longer routes than the initial limit. TRAP: Assuming the bar depletes linearly without considering refill timing led to wasted moves on inefficient probes.

GOAL: Move the yellow plug to the first platform and the green plug to the last platform by adjusting the widths of four adjacent zones. CONTROLS: Arrow buttons shift platform boundaries. Boundary shifts push or pull the plugs. Clicking a gate opens a path for a plug to cross. RULE: Shrinking one platform always expands its neighbor. The total width of all platforms is constant. TRAP: Believing you can shrink a fully retracted platform. You must first expand it before shrinking it again to move adjacent plugs.

ESTABLISHED: The rig starts at P90. Green and red icons activate phases 1 and 2. FAILED: Navigating to P0 for phase 4 caused a no-op or misalignment. GOAL IS NOT: Placing the orange block at P0. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the rig. Clicking icons selects phases. SPACE stamps the block.

ESTABLISHED: Releasing the pink object causes it to float upward to the top of the connected water body, then sink over time. FAILED: Probing specific dirt blocks in the middle band to locate the pink object yielded no visible result or successful retrieval. GOAL IS NOT: The pink object is not simply a static item sitting in the starting pool; it moves dynamically through water channels. CONTROLS: Clicking dirt blocks carves them away, allowing water flow and releasing trapped objects, but does not directly move the player.

GOAL: Merge four small blocks into one large block to fill the progress bar. CONTROLS: Clicking near two same-sized blocks merges them into a larger block. RULE: Clicks only merge blocks if they are close enough to the click point and identical in size. TRAP: Thinking mixed-size blocks can merge; clicking near different sizes wastes time and fails.

GOAL: Guide the green token to the yellow box by rotating red bars to form a bridge across gaps. CONTROLS: Arrows move the green token; clicking red buttons rotates bars between horizontal and vertical positions. RULE: Bars must be vertical to allow horizontal movement across their columns, creating necessary paths. TRAP: Rotating bars while the token is on them causes errors; ensure the token is clear before rotating.

ESTABLISHED: Pours are one-shot tests that revert if containers remain empty. FAILED: Pouring without pre-adjusting plumbing always reverts. GOAL IS NOT: Filling containers in a single initial pour. CONTROLS: Move bar to test flow; pours swap red blocks to reshape the bar for the next attempt.

GOAL: Rotate each glyph to match its required symbol. CONTROLS: Arrows move the cursor; Up dials the selected tile. RULE: Each tile’s glyphs rotate together, so the pattern must be rotationally consistent. TRAP: Assuming any glyph sequence is reachable; only specific rotations exist, so verify the target is in the cycle before committing moves.

GOAL: Deliver the merged Y piece to cover the second ball's center. CONTROLS: Click to move small blocks, merge two small blocks into a Y, and click to move the Y toward the target. RULE: The level only completes when the Y piece fully covers the ball's center, not just when a small block is placed. TRAP: Believing that placing a small block on the ball would finish the level, causing wasted moves before realizing the Y piece is mandatory.

ESTABLISHED: A single chase entity pursues the player. The player must reach a specific target zone. The entity moves one step per turn, prioritizing vertical alignment before horizontal. FAILED: Attempting to run directly to the goal or using the bottom-left corner as a safe haven results in immediate capture due to the entity's pursuit logic. GOAL IS NOT: The target is not the bottom-left corner, nor is the entity a static obstacle that can be ignored. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the player. The chase entity automatically moves toward the player after each turn.

ESTABLISHED: Five boxes must reach the bar; one cell stays empty. Four are parked. FAILED: Standing on the bar blocks parking and causes stalls. GOAL IS NOT: Filling every cell or moving the orange. CONTROLS: Move away from the bar to a safe spot, then wait for remaining boxes to park automatically.

GOAL: Position the yellow plug segments at target columns and move the plug to the top-right zone. CONTROLS: Four buttons shifted the edges of three colored bars, changing the plug's horizontal position. RULE: The plug moves only when its yellow segments align exactly with an open gate's columns. TRAP: Assuming bar widths could not shrink to zero blocked the solution; full retraction was necessary to align the plug.

ESTABLISHED: Head movement drags the group centroid. Group size dictates head offset. FAILED: Direct greedy routing to the goal. Ignoring centroid math caused collisions. GOAL IS NOT: Simply moving the head to the exit. The blob must reach the target. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the head. Space triggers swaps.

ESTABLISHED: The plus piece slides north when pushed down from beside its top arm. FAILED: Pushing the plus south by pressing down from various positions beside its middle or top arms. GOAL IS NOT: The plus moving south via a direct downward push from its middle band. CONTROLS: Pressing down moves the green block; if its destination overlaps the plus's bounding box, the plus slides in the opposite direction if its intended path is blocked.

GOAL: Navigate the grid to the target blob and uncover the dial to reveal the correct color. CONTROLS: Arrows move the character; actions trigger cover interactions and collect rings to refill the action bar. RULE: Covering the dial cycles its color; match the revealed color to the marker’s shape to solve the level. TRAP: Ignoring the action bar limit leads to failure; collect rings early to extend your move count.

GOAL: Guide the charcoal piece to overlap the yellow target zone. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the selected piece; clicks select a different piece to control. RULE: The charcoal piece always shifts in the same direction as the currently selected piece, regardless of which one you control. TRAP: Assuming the charcoal moves independently or stays still when selecting the black piece, causing wasted moves trying to position them separately.

ESTABLISHED: The yellow state is tied to the snake's press parity, not ghost presence. Clearing ghosts via SPACE preserves the current shift state. Ghost replays toggle the button count based on their recorded paths. FAILED: Assuming ghost presence alone maintains the shift. Ignoring that replay paths must independently toggle the button to maintain parity for the player's final path. GOAL IS NOT: Simply clearing ghosts. The goal requires managing button parity through specific ghost recording routes to ensure the yellow state aligns with the player's final movement needs. CONTROLS: SPACE clea

GOAL: Slide two blocks until they crash head-on to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrow keys push both blocks simultaneously in that direction across the floor. RULE: Press toward each other when they are side-by-side to force the collision. TRAP: Assuming you must keep them in their original rows wastes moves; align them first.

GOAL: Mirror the bottom T-shape to cover the top yellow target. CONTROLS: Arrows moved pieces; clicks selected or confirmed placement. RULE: Vertical flip across the center line required the nub to sit on top. TRAP: Assuming the bar stays at the top caused misalignment with the target shape.

ESTABLISHED: The plug's tip can cover one object's cap while its body covers another's. FAILED: Connecting two caps of the same object; covering two blue caps; covering caps of all three objects. GOAL IS NOT: Simply touching any cap; connecting only yellow caps; covering every object simultaneously. CONTROLS: UP moves the plug vertically; LEFT moves it horizontally; each action costs one turn.
